plan.title: Whole-blood case vs control classifier (n=60/60)
plan.analytical_narrative: The data is a 60 vs 60 unpaired whole-blood bulk RNA-seq cohort (12000 genes x 121 columns, raw Salmon gene counts). At this sample size the standard negative-binomial DE tools (DESeq2/edgeR) are known to inflate false positives on population cohorts, so the grounded procedure routes differential expression through limma-voom with TMM normalization rather than a Wald/LRT count model. The plan first establishes sample structure (QC, PCA, outlier check) since no per-sample QC has been run yet on this profile. It then runs limma-voom DE (case vs control) to characterize what separates the groups and to sanity-check that a biological signal exists, followed by Hallmark/Reactome enrichment on the moderated-t ranked list for interpretation. Critically, the research question asks for a CLASSIFIER and an accuracy estimate on a new sample — this requires a supervised, nested cross-validated penalized logistic regression that reselects features from the full filtered gene matrix inside each fold (not from the genes called significant by the group-level limma DE, which would leak label information and produce an optimistic estimate). The classifier step reports ROC-AUC with a cross-validated confidence interval, the stability of the selected gene panel across folds, and states explicitly that performance is only as good as this internal cross-validation shows — a truly independent external cohort would be needed for a validated real-world accuracy claim. A blood-composition covariate check is included because whole-blood transcriptomes are dominated by leukocyte proportions, and a classifier that merely detects a shift in blood cell composition (rather than a disease-specific signal) is a common confound in case/control whole-blood studies.
